state_background_check.value: Ohio Revised Code 2961.01(A)(1) strips anyone convicted of a felony of the 'privilege of holding office' in the state: it makes a felon 'incompetent ... to hold an office of honor, trust, or profit.' This Ohio law does NOT reach candidates for the U.S. House or Senate, however. The Constitution's own Qualifications Clauses (Art. I, §2, cl. 2 for the House; §3, cl. 3 for the Senate) are the exclusive qualifications for Congress, and the U.S. Supreme Court held in U.S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton, 514 U.S. 779 (1995), that 'States cannot impose qualification requirements on membership in Congress' (Cornell LII, Constitution Annotated, ArtI.S3.C3.4, https://www.law.cornell.edu/constitution-conan/article-1/section-3/clause-3/states-ability-to-change-qualifications-requirements-for-senate) — changing congressional qualifications requires a constitutional amendment. The ACLU of Ohio states this plainly for the state: 'a person convicted of a felony may run for either the U.S. House or Senate so long as he or she satisfies the other requirements' because 'Congress cannot impose further restrictions on candidates without amending the U.S. Constitution' (https://www.acluohio.org/news/felon-candidacy/). Net effect: a felony conviction bars someone from Ohio state office but does NOT bar them from running for or serving in Ohio's U.S. House or Senate seats.
state_background_check.snippet: (A)(1) A person who pleads guilty to a felony under the laws of this or any other state or the United States and whose plea is accepted by the court or a person against whom a verdict or finding of guilt for committing a felony under any law of that type is returned, unless the plea, verdict, or finding is reversed or annulled, is incompetent to be an elector or juror or to hold an office of honor, trust, or profit.

bio_summary.value: Eric Conroy’s mission began on the West Side of Cincinnati, where four generations of blue-collar grit and a World War II veteran grandfather taught him that service is bigger than self. After 9/11, Eric answered his generation’s call, graduating from the U.S. Air Force Academy near the top of his class, rising to the rank of Captain in Special Operations units, and later serving with the CIA as a Case Officer where he conducted high-risk intelligence missions that kept Americans safe.

bio_summary.value: Gregory John Landsman (born December 4, 1976) [ 1 ] is an American politician who has been the U.S. representative from Ohio's 1st congressional district since 2023. The district is based in Cincinnati , and includes most of its inner suburbs. A member of the Democratic Party , Landsman served on the Cincinnati City Council from 2018 to 2022. [ 2 ] He was elected to the United States House of Representatives in the 2022 election , defeating 13-term incumbent Steve Chabot . He is described as a centrist Democrat . [ 3 ]

platform.value: Supports responsible spending reforms to address inflation and make life more affordable for Ohioans
platform.snippet: Reckless government spending has fueled inflation, driving up the cost of groceries, housing, healthcare, childcare, and higher education. Nathan supports responsible spending reforms and policies that make homeownership more attainable, helping families keep more of what they earn and achieve long-term financial stability.

platform.value: Opposes government mass surveillance as a violation of the Fourth Amendment and believes Americans should be free from unwarranted government monitoring
platform.snippet: Government mass surveillance is dangerous. Not only is it a violation of the Fourth Amendment and individual privacy rights, but it also creates cybersecurity risks, undermines personal autonomy, and increases the potential for abuse by law enforcement and others with access to sensitive information. Nathan believes that Americans should be free from unwarranted government monitoring and that constitutional protections against unreasonable searches and surveillance must be upheld.

platform.value: Supports ending ongoing foreign wars, commits to rejecting future unjust wars, and believes the United States should reduce the number of its active military bases abroad
platform.snippet: Nathan supports ending ongoing foreign wars, commits to rejecting future unjust wars, and believes the United States should reduce the number of its active military bases abroad. In his view, there is no reason for the United States to serve as the world police.

platform.value: Supports an Ellis Island-style immigration policy that makes entry into the United States easier and provides a simple path to permanent residency, supports eliminating the militarization of border security and immigration enforcement
platform.snippet: Nathan supports an Ellis Island-style immigration policy that makes entry into the United States easier and provides a simple path to permanent residency. He supports eliminating the militarization of border security and immigration enforcement, believing that force should not be used against individuals who are not violent.

platform.value: Supports abolishing ICE and replacing it with nothing
platform.snippet: Abolish ICE and replacing it with nothing.

bio_summary.value: For most of my life, I have watched government grow while the liberties promised to all fade away. Trillions of dollars have been spent on wars across the world while surveillance has expanded across the United States. The promise of a better future has been thrown away to benefit those in power, while everyday Ohioans struggle to make ends meet. It was never meant to be this way. The status quo created these problems, and it will not solve them. Washington needs a change in leadership, a new generation that is willing to go against the political establishment, defend our constitutional freedoms, and fight for the liberties of all people. I am prepared to be that change. I am running to represent the people of Southwest Ohio - not only AIPAC donors or MAGA supporters.
